ucs.title: [LLM] Patchwork (Dropping Elephant) CVE-2017-11882 EQNEDT32.EXE → script/LOLBin child chain
ucs.description: Hunts Patchwork's signature initial-access chain: weaponised RTF/DOCX exploiting Microsoft Equation Editor (CVE-2017-11882 / CVE-2018-0802) where EQNEDT32.EXE spawns a shell, LOLBin or scripting host. Patchwork has used this lure pattern against South-Asian government, diplomatic and defence targets for years (BadNews / EHDevel / NDiskMonitor / Bezigate loaders).
ucs.splunk: | tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_hash) as process_hash values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="EQNEDT32.EXE" (Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","hh.exe","msiexec.exe") OR Processes.process IN ("*http://*","*https://*","*-EncodedCommand*","*-enc *","*DownloadString*","*FromBase64String*","*AppData\\Local\\Temp*","*ProgramData*")) by host Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "eqnedt32.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","hh.exe","msiexec.exe")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","DownloadString","FromBase64String","AppData\\Local\\Temp","ProgramData")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\EQNEDT32.EXE"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe","\\hh.exe","\\msiexec.exe")
    or CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","DownloadString","FromBase64String","AppData\\Local\\Temp","ProgramData")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Patchwork CVE-2017-11882 EQNEDT32.EXE Suspicious Child Process
id: 7c5e4a92-9dcb-4f31-b7b8-9a3d2b9b6f10
status: experimental
description: Detects Microsoft Equation Editor (EQNEDT32.EXE) spawning a shell, LOLBin or scripting host - the signature exploit chain used by Patchwork (Dropping Elephant) against South Asian diplomatic / defence targets.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0040/
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2017-11882
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026-05-28
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1566.001
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.g0040
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\EQNEDT32.EXE'
  selection_child_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\hh.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  selection_child_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp'
      - '\ProgramData'
  condition: selection_parent and (selection_child_image or selection_child_cmd)
falsepositives:
  - Office add-in installers (rare; should be baselined)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\EQNEDT32.EXE OR *\\eqnedt32.exe) (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RunDll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\RegSvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\hh.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*http\://* OR *https\://* OR *-EncodedCommand* OR *DownloadString* OR *FromBase64String* OR *AppData\\Local\\Temp* OR *ProgramData*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/eqnedt32\.exe/i
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|mshta|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|hh|msiexec)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/(https?:\/\/|-EncodedCommand|-enc\s|DownloadString|FromBase64String|\\AppData\\Local\\Temp|\\ProgramData)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: EQNEDT32.EXE has no legitimate business spawning shells, scripting hosts or LOLBins — its only normal child is itself or winword.exe. Patchwork has leaned on CVE-2017-11882/CVE-2018-0802 maldocs as a primary delivery vector for almost a decade (BadNews loaders, EHDevel, NDiskMonitor) because their South-Asian government targets run unpatched Office. ucs.title: [LLM] Patchwork BadNews dead-drop resolver — non-browser fetch from public paste/code-hosting C2 caches
ucs.description: Hunts the BadNews loader's hallmark behaviour: a non-browser process retrieves a small, often base64/hex-encoded blob from a hard-coded URL on a legitimate public service (Github raw/gist, Pastebin, Blogspot, Feed43, WordPress) to learn the real C2 endpoint. This dead-drop resolver pattern (T1102.001) has appeared in every BadNews variant tracked since 2013 and remains a Patchwork-specific operational fingerprint.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.user) as user values(Web.dest) as dest values(Web.src) as src from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*raw.githubusercontent.com*" OR Web.url="*gist.githubusercontent.com*" OR Web.url="*pastebin.com/raw*" OR Web.url="*paste.ee/r*" OR Web.url="*hastebin.com/raw*" OR Web.url="*blogspot.*" OR Web.url="*feed43.com*" OR Web.url="*files.wordpress.com*") NOT (Web.app IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe") OR Web.process IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","git.exe","code.exe")) by host Web.src Web.dest Web.user Web.app Web.url Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ucs.kql:
let DeadDropHosts = dynamic(["raw.githubusercontent.com","gist.githubusercontent.com","pastebin.com","paste.ee","hastebin.com","blogspot.com","feed43.com","files.wordpress.com"]);
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","git.exe","code.exe","slack.exe","teams.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (DeadDropHosts)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (Browsers)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | project DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId = ProcessId, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
  ) on DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), Hits = count(), SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentImage
| where Hits >= 1
| order by FirstSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let DeadDropHosts = dynamic(["raw.githubusercontent.com","gist.githubusercontent.com","pastebin.com","paste.ee","hastebin.com","blogspot.com","feed43.com","files.wordpress.com"]);
let Browsers = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","iexplore.exe","safari.exe","git.exe","code.exe","slack.exe","teams.exe"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has_any (DeadDropHosts) or HttpHostName in~ (DeadDropHosts)
| extend ProcName = tolower(tostring(split(SrcProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where isempty(ProcName) or ProcName !in (Browsers)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcProcessName, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstIpAddr
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@DestinationHostname:(*raw.githubusercontent.com OR *gist.githubusercontent.com OR *pastebin.com OR *paste.ee OR *hastebin.com OR *blogspot.com OR *feed43.com OR *files.wordpress.com)) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\Chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\MSEdge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\Firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\opera.exe OR *\\iexplore.exe OR *\\IEXPLORE.EXE OR *\\git.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\slack.exe OR *\\Teams.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(raw\.githubusercontent\.com|gist\.githubusercontent\.com|pastebin\.com|paste\.ee|hastebin\.com|blogspot\.com|feed43\.com|files\.wordpress\.com)$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera|iexplore|safari|git|code|slack|teams)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| sort(_count, order=desc)

That design lets the operators rotate C2 without redistributing the implant.
